raw:
In 2020, the pole sitter won 10 of the 17 races.

I checked each race's top-10 report for the starting grid position of the winner. Where the winner started from grid 1, the race counts:

| Round | Race | Winner (grid) | Pole win? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Austrian | Bottas (1) | Yes |
| 2 | Styrian | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 3 | Hungarian | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 4 | British | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 5 | 70th Anniversary | Verstappen (4) | No |
| 6 | Spanish | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 7 | Belgian | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 8 | Italian | Gasly (10) | No |
| 9 | Tuscan | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 10 | Russian | Bottas (3) | No |
| 11 | Eifel | Hamilton (2) | No |
| 12 | Portuguese | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 13 | Emilia Romagna | Hamilton (2) | No |
| 14 | Turkish | Hamilton (6) | No |
| 15 | Bahrain | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 16 | Sakhir | Pérez (5) | No |
| 17 | Abu Dhabi | Verstappen (1) | Yes |

The season standings (Hamilton 11 wins, Bottas 2, Verstappen 2, Pérez 1, Gasly 1) are consistent with these results. Two caveats: the Eifel row is inferred from Hamilton starting 2nd, since the report doesn't list the pole sitter, and Austria's pole sitter is inferred from Bottas starting 1st.

ANSWER: 10
